purpose: A deliberately ambiguous extraction candidate that deterministic validation must route to quarantine rather than publish.

candidate.proposed_methodology: Treat the issuer's composite non-valuation servicing expense measure as servicing operating expense.
candidate.evidence_locator: Servicing Segment Highlights table, page 4, 2Q26 column

bounded_exact_excerpt.normalization: SEC-furnished HTML table text with whitespace and column separators normalized; labels and displayed values are unchanged.
bounded_exact_excerpt.text:
Profitability (in millions) | 2Q26 | 1Q26 | 2Q25
Operating expenses | 76 | 81 | 77
Payoff-related expenses | 29 | 31 | 17
Credit losses and provisions for defaulted loans | 26 | 23 | 22
Interest expense | 140 | 125 | 130
Expenses excluding valuation-related items | 270 | 260 | 246

conflicts_and_uncertainties: The raw label is a composite non-GAAP presentation, not the catalog label servicing operating expense.
The composite includes payoff-related expense, credit losses and provisions for defaulted loans, and interest expense in addition to the separately labeled Operating expenses row.
The displayed Q2 2026 components sum to 271 while the displayed composite total is 270 because the source is rounded to whole millions; exact-dollar reconciliation is unavailable from this excerpt.
Publishing the composite as servicing_operating_expense would silently broaden that metric's inclusion rules.
required_review_questions: Should servicing_operating_expense map only to the separately labeled Operating expenses row?
Should the composite receive a separate versioned metric definition for expenses excluding valuation-related items?
Can a filed segment table or deterministic reconciliation establish exact inclusion rules without relying on the earnings-release shorthand?
candidate.must_not_publish_reason: Metric identity and inclusion rules are unresolved. Missing semantic resolution must not be converted into an authoritative observation.
